summary: Miles audio stream volume-control entry. Calls CorruptedThunk, then dispatches through a vtable-style object in ecx (v2): invokes the method at vtable slot +8 with a1, and only on a non-zero result reads a stream pointer at v2+12. If the stream pointer is non-zero and the volume argument a2 is 0.0, calls the method at vtable slot +12 on the object (stream control path); otherwise calls the AIL_set_stream_volume_levels import with the stream and the volume float read at v2+4, returning the import's result.

local_names.a1: handle/argument forwarded to the vtable slot +8 method
local_names.a2: volume level argument; 0.0 selects the vtable slot +12 control path
local_names.v2: audio object with a vtable pointer at +0 and per-stream volume at +4
local_names.v3: alias of v2 used after the slot +8 call

operations.description: Read the vtable pointer at v2+0 and store the saved return address into v2+4 (decompiler __userpurge frame artifact)
Indirect stdcall call of the method at vtable slot +8 (*(*(v2)+8)) with a1; the result gates the rest of the function
Only when the slot +8 call result is non-zero is the stream path evaluated; otherwise the function returns that result
Read the stream pointer v6 at v3+12
Stream path proceeds only while the stream pointer v6 is non-zero
When a2 == 0.0 the vtable slot +12 method is dispatched instead of the volume-levels import
Indirect thiscall of the method at vtable slot +12 (*(*(v3)+12)) on v3, returned directly (stream control / mute path)
AIL_set_stream_volume_levels(v6, v3[1], v3[1]) applies the volume float read at v3+4 to both channels of the stream; result returned
Return the slot +8 result when the stream pointer guard fails

unresolved: The write of the saved return address into v2+4 and the provenance of v2 (ecx-passed __userpurge object) are decompiler artifacts; because v3[1] reads that same slot, the exact volume value passed to AIL_set_stream_volume_levels cannot be trusted
The purpose of the vtable slot +12 call versus the AIL import path (mute vs level-set) is inferred, not documented
